doc.title: Carmen Lundy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 15, 2023

title: Asked to change her name, then deciding to move to New York
summary: The hotel president asked her to change her name; she declined. Friends left for New York and she moved in 1978 after a year at Monty Trainer's.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: for that gig there was a meeting. The president of the hotel wanted to talk to me without the band, okay? This was kind of scary, you know you do your audition, you do your four or five songs and then the owner of the hotel wants to talk to you. So I go into his office and he was very, very, you know I guess very classy fellow he was, and he just said, “Well we were wondering, Miss Lundy, would you consider changing your name?” Because the room that I would be playing for that full year is called the Mona Lisa Lounge or something like that. It wasn’t the main stage where the Smothers Brothers and Jackie Gleason and all those people played, okay? But it was inside this major hotel in Miami Beach. He asked me, “Would you consider changing your name to Mona?” And I thought — and there’s no one else there, it’s like the band’s not there. So I just kind of said to him, “No, sir, I really don’t think so.” Right? So I leave the meeting thinking oh no, I’ve lost the gig for everybody. You know? We don’t have the gig now because I didn’t agree to change my name to Mona, but we ultimately did get the gig and so from that point, so imagine nine to one I’ve got to drive all the way to Miami Beach every night and drive home every night, and get up for that 8:30 theory class. And I did that for a year, you understand? For years. So when it came time, now school is kind of ending and I’m looking and I go, “What happened to Pat Metheny?” “Oh he left and moved to New York.” “Well where is Mark Egan?” “Oh he moved to New York.” “Oh well where’s Patty Scialfa?” “Oh she moved to New York.” And where is da-da-da — oh they moved to New York. “Where’s Hiram? Hiram Bullock?” “Oh he moved to New York.” I’m thinking what is this New York thing and what is everybody doing going to this New York place? What is it? I mean I’m a sheltered kid. I don’t know anything about New York I mean except for the Empire State Building or whatever. I didn’t know there was this, this was the hub of the jazz world. I had no idea. When I listened to music I would listen to the music, I wasn’t listening to where they were playing or where they were recording you know. And so I made a decision on the very last engagement that I had that was a full year in Coconut Grove at a place called Monty Trainer’s Village Inn which is around the corner from the Coconut Grove Playhouse. It’s where I was introduced to black Broadway. I decided that I was going to make this move. So that’s what I did. So in 1978 I moved to New York and guess what happened? I walked right in to a full time weekend performance for a whole year at a club on 23rd Street in Manhattan called Jazzmania. And Jazzmania there was a time in New York where there were a lot of loft venues. So you’d go to outside of the Village Vanguard, the Village Gate and all the major venues there were these loft venues popping up everywhere. And I played Jazzmania.
